matches.rationale: Ground truth describes an overstatement in the Abstract compared to later detailed results; no finding addresses this Abstract-vs-body discrepancy. Finding 2 is about Table 2 vs Figure 4, not the Abstract.

Ground truth identifies an error/inconsistency in Proposition 2's condition number bound. Finding 1 detects a mismatch between Proposition 2's stated bound and the proof in Appendix C, capturing the same logical error.

Ground truth concerns omission of hyperparameters and reproducibility details. No finding reports missing hyperparameter transparency; finding 3 addresses a different design flaw (asymmetric adversarial training).
Ground truth concerns overstatement in the Conclusion of combined metric performance and societal claims. None of the findings mention the Conclusion or its exaggerated claims.

Ground truth describes fabricated citations/misattributions in the Related Work section. Finding 5 points to mislabeling of LoRA in an experimental table, which is a different location and a different type of misrepresentation.
Ground truth is about missing ethical implications in the Experiments section. No finding discusses omission of ethical risks or limitations.
Ground truth is about promotional and exaggerated rhetorical tone in the Introduction. No finding identifies rhetorical manipulation or overhyped language in the Introduction.

Ground truth describes an incoherence between the orthogonality assumption and the algorithmic steps (diagonal S, truncation). Finding 4 is about undefined notation (L̃) and Finding 6 is about an algebraic error in Appendix C; neither addresses this algorithmic inconsistency.

Ground truth states tabulated numbers (accuracy etc.) were manipulated by a few percentage points in the Experiments. Finding 2 detects a 2% discrepancy in clean accuracy between Table 2 and Figure 4, directly evidencing data integrity issues.

Ground truth is about exaggerated interpretation of gains ('almost doubles' baseline accuracy) in the Experiments discussion. No finding addresses this specific overstatement or speculative attribution.

Ground truth identifies asymmetric adversarial training exposure biasing comparisons. Finding 3 explicitly states baseline/DLRT were trained on clean data while RobustDLRT used adversarial batches, making the comparison invalid—exactly the same protocol flaw.
Ground truth concerns implausibly low training time overhead and missing benchmarking details. No finding discusses training runtime or computational cost benchmarks.

Ground truth points out a contradiction between the Abstract's claim of being model-agnostic and the Method's restriction to Tucker factorization. No finding mentions this abstract-method incoherence.
Ground truth is about omission of ethical statements in the Appendix. No finding addresses ethical considerations or omissions in the Appendix.
